page.title: 1 · Create demand
page.description: Schaefer momentum, the schedule drop, bobblehead production and group holds at UBS Arena. Public facts cited; operational flows and uncited figures are illustrative.

sections.heading: The Schaefer effect
text: How a team sells, fills and follows up on a season of seats at UBS Arena, from the 2025 Schaefer demand surge to next year's renewal, told with the New York Islanders' public promotions. Public facts are cited on each step (open the green markers); the ticketing, CRM, app, scanning and POS flows are illustrative reconstructions, not any team's or vendor's systems, and figures are illustrative unless a source is given.
bullets: The **fact tiles** light one at a time, each with its date; dimmed tiles have no claim yet
The **300 level** fills section by section as each fact lands (illustrative): sidelines first, then corners, then the far ends
The **crowd tiles** track the illustrative crowd against about 17,250 seats

**Season at a glance, across all four arcs:** Jun 27, 2025 the No. 1 pick · Jul 24, 2026 single-game on-sale · Aug 25 promo schedule · Oct 22 a friend's ticket · Nov 7 hat night · Nov 27 Sorokin night · Dec 1 GOAT USA Night · Feb 13, 2027 Schaefer bobblehead · Mar 27 Greek Heritage Night · renewal and All-Star 2027

initial.note: Capacities are an illustrative even split of 17,250 seats over 80 sections.

steps.text: **Start from a soft night.** The lowest Islanders crowd in UBS Arena history as of October 2024 was **12,739**, a Tuesday against Detroit ([Isles Fix](https://www.islesfix.com/p/taking-attendance)). The split by section is illustrative: the 300 level is about two-thirds empty. Eight fact tiles wait, dimmed.

map.note: A soft weeknight. The 12,739 total is sourced (Isles Fix, Oct 2024); the split by section is illustrative. Capacities are an illustrative even split of 17,250 over 80 sections.

steps.text: **2025: the lottery.** The Islanders win the draft lottery from **3.5%** odds ([TSN](https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/new-york-islanders-win-draft-lottery-will-select-first-overall-in-2025-nhl-draft-1.2301275)). Nothing new is on sale yet, but the news goes to every fan on file, and the first 300-level sidelines fill (illustrative).

map.note: Illustrative: interest shows first in the cheapest seats with the best view, the 300-level sidelines.

deltaLinks.label: TSN, Islanders win the 2025 draft lottery

steps.text: **Jun 27, 2025: the No. 1 pick.** The club takes **Matthew Schaefer** first overall, its first No. 1 pick since John Tavares in 2009 ([IIHF](https://canada-central.iihf.com/en/news/68829/islanders_draft_matthew_schaefer_first_overall)). Every message now has a face, and each one carries a buy link into ticketing.

map.note: Illustrative: two more 300-level sideline sections fill.

deltaLinks.label: IIHF, Islanders draft Schaefer first overall

steps.text: **Dec 18, 2025: jerseys first.** Kelly Cheeseman, president of business operations, reports jersey sales **up 63%** year over year, Schaefer the top seller; the team ran out of 4s and 8s to make jerseys ([NY Post via AOL](https://www.aol.com/news/islanders-matthew-schaefer-effect-real-002411744.html)). Merchandise moves first: a jersey is one click, a ticket is a night out.

map.note: Illustrative: the last 300-level sideline sections start to fill.

deltaLinks.label: NY Post via AOL, the Schaefer effect (Dec 18, 2025)

steps.text: **Same report: tickets up 7%.** The article gives no comparison period for this figure, so read it as direction, not a rate. New buyers flow from ticketing back into the CRM, where they become next season's prospects.

map.note: “We have a legitimate chance to sell out every game until the Olympic break.” Kelly Cheeseman, NY Post via AOL, Dec 18, 2025. Section fills remain illustrative.

deltaLinks.label: NY Post via AOL, the Schaefer effect (Dec 18, 2025)

steps.text: **Same report: reach.** Broadcast viewership is **up 37%**, viewers aged 25 to 54 **up 58%**, and social engagement **up 40%** ([NY Post via AOL](https://www.aol.com/news/islanders-matthew-schaefer-effect-real-002411744.html)). A bigger audience means more people to segment and send to. The 300-level corners begin to fill (illustrative).

deltaLinks.label: NY Post via AOL, the Schaefer effect (Dec 18, 2025)

steps.text: **May 13, 2026: a unanimous Calder.** Schaefer wins the rookie award with **198 of 198** first-place votes, the youngest winner ever (18 years, 223 days), after 59 points ([NHL.com](https://nhl.com/news/new-york-islanders-matthew-schaefer-wins-2026-calder-trophy)). The team missed the playoffs, so the rookie carries the renewal pitch.

map.note: Illustrative: the 300-level corners are nearly gone; only the far ends stay soft.

steps.text: **Aug 25, 2026: the moment gets a date.** The 2026-27 promotional schedule names **Sat Feb 13, 2027 vs Minnesota** as Schaefer bobblehead night, for **all fans**, presented by **Northwell** ([Islanders](https://nhl.com/islanders/tickets/promotional-schedule)). Promotions agrees item, logo and count with the sponsor before a ticket for that night sells.

map.note: The bowl holds steady: this step is a plan, not a sale. Feb 13, 2027 is a sourced date; every fill shown is illustrative.

steps.text: **Feb 13, 2027: a dated product.** Promotions tags the event in ticketing and email sells *that night*: a date, a bobblehead for every fan, a sponsor, one buy link. The far 300-level ends are the last soft seats (fills illustrative). A player's year is now something a fan can put on a calendar.

map.note: Feb 13, 2027 vs MIN, Schaefer bobblehead for all fans (Northwell): sourced. The 16,500 forecast and every section fill: illustrative.

sections.heading: The 120-day bobblehead clock
text: An all-fans bobblehead night is a supply chain with a fixed end date. Working back from Sat Feb 13, 2027, four lanes run in parallel: sponsor and licensing approvals, production, freight, and event ops. Each lane has a *last safe change* date, after which a change costs the night.

The lanes table shows each lane's *last safe change* and its status; the checks show each gate; the budget shows the 172 days from announcement to game night running out and the schedule slack being spent. Pick a path to see freight arrive or slip.
bullets: **Public facts:** the Schaefer bobblehead for all fans on Feb 13 vs MIN, presented by Northwell ([NHL.com](https://www.nhl.com/islanders/news/new-york-islanders-promotional-giveaways-include-schaefer-sorokin-bobbleheads-exclusive-home-opener-t-shirt)); about 120 days to manufacture ([MASN](https://masnsports.com/blog/behind-the-scenes-of-the-bobblehead-giveaway)); a late delivery (Yankees, [NPR](https://www.npr.org/sections/thetwo-way/2013/09/25/226071535/yankees-bobble-the-ball-on-mariano-rivera-give-away-night)); digital vouchers (Pirates, [CBS Pittsburgh](https://www.cbsnews.com/pittsburgh/news/the-pirates-are-giving-paul-skenes-bobblehead-vouchers)).
**Illustrative:** every date after Aug 25, the 18,000 quantity, case counts, transit time, slack and the redemption window. No Islanders vendor, freight or ops detail is claimed.
**The lesson:** the approval lane spends slack first, and the voucher plan is cheapest when it is written before T-30.

sections.heading: Holds that quietly expire
text: A group hold takes seats off sale before anyone has paid for them. It is borrowed inventory with an expiry date, and on that date it either converts to sold or goes back on sale. This section follows three holds on one game and forks at the final-payment date.

Section numbering is from public seating guides; capacities are an illustrative even split of 17,250 seats over 80 sections. The groups, deposits, sales and prices are illustrative. The group bar near Sec 210 is a [sourced 2026-27 announcement](https://www.nhl.com/islanders/news/islanders-unveil-new-fan-experiences-ahead-of-2026-27-season-x1088). The ticketing, CRM and reporting flow is an illustrative reconstruction, not any team's or vendor's system.
bullets: Hatched sections are held: they count against capacity but not against sold
Choose **Converts** or **Expires silently** below the step controls; both paths share the first six steps

panels.title: UBS Arena, Elmont, NY · capacities illustrative

initial.note: Group sales has not placed any holds yet.

steps.text: Three weeks out, group sales holds **600 seats in 312–314** for a school group until **T-7d**, the final-payment date. Hatched seats are off sale but **not sold**.

holds.note: Each hold has an expiry: the final-payment date.

steps.text: A youth hockey club holds **260 seats in 320–321** on the same terms. Both blocks sit in the 300 level, the slowest-selling ring.

steps.deltaText: Sourced: for 2026-27 the Islanders announced a new private bar for groups of 50 to 75 near Sec 210. The corporate group booked into it is illustrative.
steps.text: A corporate outing of **70** books the new private bar for groups of 50 to 75 near **Sec 210** ([announced for 2026-27](https://www.nhl.com/islanders/news/islanders-unveil-new-fan-experiences-ahead-of-2026-27-season-x1088)). Its seats are held in 210.

steps.deltaText: Deposit models are published group policies of other clubs: a $200 non-refundable deposit to hold a date (an older Cleveland Guardians group-policy page) and a 20% deposit with full payment 45 days out (Atlanta Braves). The amounts in this table are illustrative.
steps.text: Deposits post: the youth club pays a flat **$200**, the corporate outing **20%** (models the [Guardians](https://www.mlb.com/guardians/tickets/group-tickets/policies) and [Braves](https://www.mlb.com/braves/tickets/group-tickets/pricing) publish). The school's is **pending** on a district PO.

holds.note: Deposits are illustrative, modelled on published policies of other clubs.

steps.text: Each night pricing pulls a **snapshot** of holds. Held seats look committed, so the upper-deck offer skips 312–314 and 320–321.
**T-7d, final payment.** The youth club and the corporate outing pay in full and turn sold. The school hold is left: pick **Converts** or **Expires silently**.
The district's PO clears that afternoon. Group sales converts the hold before midnight: **600 seats in 312–314 turn sold** and no hatches remain.
Ticketing **bulk-transfers** the 600 tickets to the leader's app account. The leader forwards them to families; any not forwarded by doors become a gate line.

holds.note: Delivery is a bulk transfer to each group's leader.

steps.text: Recap. Tonight's snapshot matches ticketing: **0 held**, and 312–314 show full on the sold map because every group seat is now paid revenue. When holds convert, a stale report does no harm.
Midnight passes unpaid. Ticketing **releases the hold on its own**: the hatch clears and 600 seats go back on sale. No notice reaches group sales or pricing.

holds.note: The school hold expired. Nobody was told.

steps.text: Pricing's report still shows the 600 as **held**. To the desk 312–314 is full, so the offer goes out **without** the 630 seats that are actually open.
Game night: 312–314 was never offered and draws only walk-ups. The fix is process, not price: **a hold expiry should be an event** that alerts sales, pricing and marketing.
